packages.name: com.landawn.abacus.jdbc

types.name: AbstractQuery
types.javadoc_summary: Abstract base class for JDBC query operations that provides a fluent API for executing SQL queries and updates with PreparedStatement.

methods.name: closeAfterExecution
methods.signature: public This closeAfterExecution(final boolean closeAfterExecution)

params.name: closeAfterExecution
params.javadoc: if {@code true} , the statement will be closed after execution. Default is {@code true} .

methods.javadoc_summary: Sets whether the PreparedStatement should be closed after execution.
methods.returns: this AbstractQuery instance for method chaining
contract: Sets whether the PreparedStatement should be closed after execution.
Set to {@code false} if you want to reuse the statement for multiple executions, but ensure you manually close it when done.
Result sets consumed by materializing operations are closed even when this flag is {@code false} ; streams must still be closed by their caller.

methods.javadoc_summary: Attempts to acquire a distributed lock on the specified target resource using default settings.
methods.returns: a unique {@code String} code representing the acquired lock, or {@code null} if the lock could not be acquired within the default timeout, or if the calling thread was interrupted while waiting (in which case the thread's interrupt status is preserved).
contract: If the lock is successfully acquired, a unique lock code is returned, which must be used to release the lock later.
If the lock cannot be acquired within the timeout, {@code null} is returned.

Usage Examples: 

 {@code try (DBLock dbLock = JdbcUtil.createDBLock(dataSource, "my_locks_table")) { String resourceIdentifier = "report_generation_task"; String lockCode = dbLock.tryLock(resourceIdentifier); if (lockCode != null) { try { System.out.println("Lock acquired for: " + resourceIdentifier); // Perform the critical operation that requires exclusive access // ...

} finally { // Ensure the lock is released, even if an error occurs dbLock.unlock(resourceIdentifier, lockCode); System.out.println("Lock released for: " + resourceIdentifier); } } else { System.out.println("Failed to acquire lock for: " + resourceIdentifier + " within default timeout."); } } }

methods.javadoc_summary: Attempts to acquire a distributed lock on the specified target resource with full control over lock duration, acquisition timeout, and retry behavior.
methods.returns: a unique {@code String} code representing the acquired lock, or {@code null} if the lock could not be acquired before {@code timeout} elapsed or before the internal attempt-count safeguard (derived from {@code timeout / retryInterval} ) was exhausted, or if the calling thread was interrupted while waiting (in which case the thread's interrupt status is preserved). A failure of an individual acquisition attempt is logged, not thrown.
contract: If the initial attempt fails (meaning another process holds the lock), it will repeatedly retry after {@code retryInterval} milliseconds until the total {@code timeout} is reached.
If the calling thread is interrupted while sleeping between attempts, the loop stops immediately, the thread's interrupt status is restored, and {@code null} is returned.
When the timeout elapses without success, {@code null} is returned and the last failure (if any) is logged.

Usage Examples: 

 {@code try (DBLock dbLock = JdbcUtil.createDBLock(dataSource, "my_locks_table")) { String resourceIdentifier = "inventory_update_process"; long lockDuration = 5 * 60 * 1000; // Lock for 5 minutes long acquisitionTimeout = 10 * 1000; // Wait up to 10 seconds long retryInterval = 500; // Retry every 500 milliseconds String lockCode = dbLock.tryLock(resourceIdentifier, lockDuration, acquisitionTimeout, retryInterval); if (lockCode != null) { try { System.out.println("Lock acquired for: " + resourceIdentifier); // Perform the inventory update // ...

contract: This method is useful when you need to reuse a PreparedStatement or have specific statement configuration requirements.

Performance tips:

  • Larger batch sizes generally improve performance but consume more memory
  • Batch intervals can help prevent database overload during massive imports
  • Consider the database's maximum packet size when setting batch size

Usage Examples: 

 {@code // Import with transaction control and prepared statement reuse Connection conn = dataSource.getConnection(); conn.setAutoCommit(false); PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement( "INSERT INTO orders (order_id, customer_id, total, status) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)"); try { // Import pending orders Iterator pendingOrders = getPendingOrders(); long pending = DataTransferUtil.importData(pendingOrders, stmt, 1000, 0, (query, order) -> { query.setLong(1, order.getId()); query.setLong(2, order.getCustomerId()); query.setBigDecimal(3, order.getTotal()); query.setString(4, "PENDING"); }); // Reuse statement for completed orders Iterator completedOrders = getCompletedOrders(); long completed = DataTransferUtil.importData(completedOrders, stmt, 1000, 0, (query, order) -> { query.setLong(1, order.getId()); query.setLong(2, order.getCustomerId()); query.setBigDecimal(3, order.getTotal()); query.setString(4, "COMPLETED"); }); conn.commit(); System.out.println("Imported " + pending + " pending and " + completed + " completed orders"); } catch (Exception e) { conn.rollback(); throw e; } finally { stmt.close(); conn.close(); } }

methods.name: to
methods.signature: @SequentialOnly @Stateful static <T> BiRowMapper<T> to(final Class<? extends T> targetClass, final Predicate<? super String> columnNameFilter, final Function<? super String, String> columnNameConverter, final boolean ignoreUnmatchedColumns) throws IllegalArgumentException

params.name: targetClass
params.javadoc: the class to map rows to (bean, array, {@code Map} , {@code List} , or single-column scalar type)

params.name: columnNameFilter
params.javadoc: a predicate to filter which columns should be considered for mapping; may be {@code null} , in which case all columns are considered

params.name: columnNameConverter
params.javadoc: a function to transform column names before matching them to properties; may be {@code null} , in which case the original column name is used

params.name: ignoreUnmatchedColumns
params.javadoc: if {@code true} , columns that pass the filter but cannot be matched to a property of {@code targetClass} are silently skipped; if {@code false} , an {@code IllegalArgumentException} is thrown by the returned mapper whenever initialization encounters an unmatched column (only relevant for bean targets).

throws.condition: if {@code targetClass} is {@code null} or a bean target has conflicting or invalid property metadata, or if a non-trivial {@code columnNameFilter} / {@code columnNameConverter} is supplied together with a single-column scalar {@code targetClass} (which does not support filtering or conversion).

methods.javadoc_summary: Creates a stateful {@code BiRowMapper} with full customization over column filtering, name conversion, and handling of non-matched columns.
methods.returns: a new stateful {@code BiRowMapper} . Do not cache or reuse across different query structures.
contract: It should not be cached, shared across different query structures, or used in parallel streams.

Positional targets represent a filtered-out column differently: for an array target the column keeps its original index and its slot is left {@code null} , while for a {@code List} target the column is omitted entirely (the list is compacted, so list index no longer equals column index when a filter drops columns).
If a filter, converter, or property lookup fails, the next invocation retries configuration.

fields.name: TO_MAP
fields.value: (rs,columnLabels)->{ final int columnCount = columnLabels.size(); final Map<String, Object> result = N.newHashMap(columnCount); for (int i = 1; i <= columnCount; i++) { result.put(columnLabels.get(i - 1), JdbcUtil.getColumnValue(rs, i)); } return result; }

fields.name: TO_LINKED_HASH_MAP
fields.value: (rs,columnLabels)->{ final int columnCount = columnLabels.size(); final Map<String, Object> result = N.newLinkedHashMap(columnCount); for (int i = 1; i <= columnCount; i++) { result.put(columnLabels.get(i - 1), JdbcUtil.getColumnValue(rs, i)); } return result; }

fields.name: TO_ENTITY_ID
fields.value: (rs,columnLabels)->{ final int columnCount = columnLabels.size(); final Seid entityId = Seid.of(Strings.EMPTY); for (int i = 1; i <= columnCount; i++) { entityId.set(columnLabels.get(i - 1), JdbcUtil.getColumnValue(rs, i)); } return entityId; }

contract: Position {@code i} in the output array (0-based) is populated using the {@code ColumnGetter} configured for column {@code i + 1} (or the default getter if none was configured).
It should be built for each execution context and must not be cached or shared across incompatible queries or used in parallel streams.

Note: the returned extractor's {@code accept} method throws an {@link IllegalArgumentException} if the supplied result set or output array is {@code null} , the output array is shorter than the result set's column count, or a configured column index exceeds that count.
SQL errors occur when {@code accept} reads the metadata or column values, rather than when this builder method is called.

types.name: DaoCache
types.javadoc_summary: An interface for caching the results of DAO method calls.

methods.name: create
methods.signature: static DaoCache create(final int capacity, final long evictDelay) throws IllegalArgumentException, IllegalStateException

params.name: capacity
params.javadoc: the maximum number of entries in the cache.

params.name: evictDelay
params.javadoc: the interval in milliseconds for the eviction scheduler to run.

throws.condition: if {@code capacity} or {@code evictDelay} is negative.
if JVM shutdown has begun and the backing pool cannot register its shutdown hook.

methods.javadoc_summary: Creates a {@code DaoCache} with a specified capacity and eviction delay, backed by a {@link DefaultDaoCache} which uses a {@link KeyedObjectPool} for in-memory caching with TTL and idle time-based eviction.
methods.returns: a new {@code DaoCache} instance.
contract: Its pool registers a JVM shutdown hook and, when {@code evictDelay} is positive, runs a periodic eviction task; the hook closes the pool when the JVM exits, and {@link DefaultDaoCache#close()} releases both earlier, once nothing uses the cache any more.

Create such a cache and its DAOs once, for as long as the application uses them, not per request or unit of work (each new cache instance registers another proxy): 

 {@code // At application startup: Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache userCache = new Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache(1000, 3000); UserDao userDao = JdbcUtil.createDao(UserDao.class, dataSource, JdbcUtil.DaoCreationOptions.builder().cache(userCache).build()); // At application shutdown (or when the application is undeployed), after the last use of userDao: userCache.close(); }

{@code DaoCache} itself declares no {@code close()} : to close a cache before the JVM exits, hold it as a {@link DefaultDaoCache} , which is {@link AutoCloseable} , as above.

contract: To reuse it multiple times with different parameters, call {@link PreparedQuery#closeAfterExecution(boolean) closeAfterExecution(false)} and close it explicitly when done.
Reusing a single statement is more efficient than creating new prepared statements for each execution, especially when the same query is executed repeatedly with different parameters.

This method intelligently manages connections: if a transaction is active on the current thread (started via {@link #beginTransaction(javax.sql.DataSource)} or Spring's transactional support), the transactional connection is used.

methods.javadoc_summary: Checks whether a table exists in the database referenced by the given {@link javax.sql.DataSource} .
methods.returns: {@code true} if the table exists, {@code false} otherwise.
contract: Delimited and case-folded parts are matched case-sensitively; upper- and lower-case table variants are tried only when the driver reports no canonical identifier case).
If metadata lookup yields no match and all parts satisfy the unquoted identifier policy, the method falls back to executing {@code SELECT 1 FROM <table> WHERE 1 > 2} .

On PostgreSQL and PostgreSQL-compatible databases (where a failed statement aborts the enclosing transaction), when the connection has auto-commit disabled, the fallback query runs under a savepoint that is rolled back if the query fails, so an expected "table not found" error does not abort the caller's transaction.
If rolling back to that savepoint fails, the transaction may be unusable, so the "table not found" error is propagated (with the rollback failure suppressed) instead of returning {@code false} .

Usage Examples: 

 {@code if (JdbcUtil.tableExists(ds, "users")) { System.out.println("Users table exists"); } else { System.out.println("Users table does not exist"); } }

This is useful for operations that must be committed immediately and independently of any surrounding transaction \u2014 for example, writing an audit log entry or updating a status flag that should survive even if the outer transaction is later rolled back.

Spring integration: When running inside a Spring-managed transaction context, Spring's transaction participation is also temporarily disabled for the duration of {@code cmd} , so the callable does not join any Spring {@code @Transactional} transaction through this library's connection-acquisition helpers.
The callback must obtain its connections through the appropriate helpers.

Usage Examples: 

 {@code // Persist an audit record that must not be rolled back with the main transaction SqlTransaction tran = JdbcUtil.beginTransaction(dataSource); try { orderDao.save(order); // part of tran String auditId = JdbcUtil.callOutsideTransaction(dataSource, () -> { // Runs on a separate connection; committed independently of 'tran' return auditDao.insertAndReturnId("ORDER_CREATED", order.getId()); }); tran.commit(); } finally { tran.rollbackIfNotCommitted(); } // No active transaction: the callback acquires connections as needed String token = JdbcUtil.callOutsideTransaction(dataSource, () -> tokenStore.generateAndPersist(userId)); }

methods.javadoc_summary: Adds a batch of parameters from an iterator for batch execution.
methods.returns: this NamedQuery instance for method chaining
contract:
Each element provided by the iterator should be a parameter object compatible with {@link #setParameters(Object)} , such as:
  • Bean objects with properties matching parameter names
  • Maps with keys matching parameter names
  • {@code Object[]} arrays or Collections for positional parameters

Repeated stream-valued names are buffered separately for each row as described in the class documentation.
The runtime type of the first element (when it is non-null) determines how the remaining non-null elements are interpreted, so they should have the same parameter shape.
If the iterator is empty, this is a no-op and no batch is added.

A {@code null} element is only supported when the SQL has exactly one parameter placeholder \u2014 a single named parameter appearing exactly once (it is bound as SQL {@code NULL} ); otherwise an {@link IllegalArgumentException} is thrown.
When the first element is {@code null} , each later non-null element is interpreted through {@link #setParameters(Object)} rather than being forced to a scalar value.
If a row is rejected or binding or queuing a row fails, this query is closed because its batch may have been only partially queued.
Consequently, missing values cannot inherit bindings from a previous row or an earlier {@code setXxx} call; each such row must supply every required value.
When the first row is a bean, bean rows are not cleared and retain pre-bound values for the reserved system date/time parameters described above.
When the first row is {@code null} , every later non-null row is bound after all current parameter bindings are cleared.

methods.javadoc_summary: Commits this transaction scope.
contract: The actual JDBC {@code COMMIT} is issued only when the outermost scope commits (reference count reaches zero).

If the transaction has been marked for rollback only (status {@link Status#MARKED_ROLLBACK} because an inner scope rolled back), the outermost commit is converted into a rollback rather than a commit; this method returns normally in that case (or throws {@link UncheckedSQLException} if that rollback itself fails).
When the outermost scope actually commits, the status transitions to {@link Status#COMMITTED} on success.

On failure the status first becomes {@link Status#FAILED_COMMIT} and an automatic rollback is attempted, leaving the status {@link Status#ROLLED_BACK} (or {@link Status#FAILED_ROLLBACK} if that rollback also fails).

After the commit attempt (success or failure) the connection's original auto-commit and isolation level are restored, and the connection is released back to its data source if this transaction was created with connection ownership.

packages.name: com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.annotation
packages.summary: Runtime annotations for declaring and configuring JDBC DAO methods.

types.name: Bind
types.javadoc_summary: Binds a method parameter to a named parameter in SQL queries.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: String value() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the named-parameter token (the part after {@code :} ) that this method parameter should be bound to in the SQL.
methods.returns: the named-parameter token to bind to (without the leading colon); empty by default
contract: Specifies the named-parameter token (the part after {@code :} ) that this method parameter should be bound to in the SQL.

An explicit value is normally required: when a named-query method has more than one statement parameter, every such parameter must carry an {@code @Bind} (or another binding annotation) with a non-empty {@code value} that matches a named parameter in the SQL verbatim.

An empty name matches no named parameter, so a named query whose {@code @Bind} names are verified against the static SQL reports {@code IllegalArgumentException} ; the binding setup that rejects an empty {@code @Bind} name outright reports {@code UnsupportedOperationException} , and is the only check left for a positional stored-procedure call or when {@link Query#fragmentsContainNamedParameters()} defers the static-SQL check.

(This differs from {@code @SqlFragment} / {@code @BindList} , where an empty value falls back to the method parameter name — which requires compiling with the {@code -parameters} flag.)

Non-empty value: on a named query a name that does not appear in the static SQL fails DAO initialization with {@code IllegalArgumentException} , while two parameters bound to the same name, or a named parameter of the SQL left unbound (the reserved system-time parameters excepted when {@link Query#injectCurrentTimeParameters()} is enabled), fail with {@code UnsupportedOperationException} .

types.name: BindList
types.javadoc_summary: Binds a collection or array parameter to a SQL query, automatically expanding it into the appropriate number of parameter placeholders.

methods.name: value
methods.signature: String value() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the template-variable name that this collection/array parameter should expand into.
methods.returns: the template-variable name; empty means use the method parameter name (requires {@code -parameters} )
contract: Specifies the template-variable name that this collection/array parameter should expand into.
The value must exactly match the template variable referenced in the {@link Query} SQL (for example, {@code @BindList("ids")} must correspond to {@code ...

If left empty, the actual method parameter name is used as the template-variable name; this requires compiling with the {@code -parameters} javac flag, otherwise initialization fails with {@code UnsupportedOperationException} .

methods.name: prefixForNonEmpty
methods.signature: @Beta String prefixForNonEmpty() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies a prefix to add before the parameter placeholder when the collection is non-empty.
methods.returns: the prefix to add when the collection is non-empty; empty (the default) means no prefix is emitted
contract: Specifies a prefix to add before the parameter placeholder when the collection is non-empty.

methods.name: suffixForNonEmpty
methods.signature: @Beta String suffixForNonEmpty() default ""
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies a suffix to add after the parameter placeholder when the collection is non-empty.
methods.returns: the suffix to add when the collection is non-empty; empty (the default) means no suffix is emitted
contract: Specifies a suffix to add after the parameter placeholder when the collection is non-empty.

types.name: Cache
types.javadoc_summary: Configures the shared DAO cache used by methods with {@link CacheResult} enabled.

methods.name: capacity
methods.signature: int capacity() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_CAPACITY
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the maximum number of entries the cache can hold.
methods.returns: the maximum number of cache entries
contract: When the cache is at capacity, the underlying pool's eviction policy determines which entries are removed to make room for new ones (the default {@link Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} relies on the {@code KeyedObjectPool} 's default policy combined with TTL/idle-time-based eviction; see {@link CacheResult#maxLiveTimeMillis()} and {@link CacheResult#maxIdleTimeMillis()} ).

methods.name: evictDelayMillis
methods.signature: long evictDelayMillis() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_EVICT_DELAY
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the interval (in milliseconds) at which the background eviction scheduler runs to remove expired entries from the cache.
methods.returns: the interval in milliseconds between eviction sweeps
contract: This is not the per-entry time-to-live; entry expiration is controlled by {@link CacheResult#maxLiveTimeMillis()} and {@link CacheResult#maxIdleTimeMillis()} when the {@link CacheResult} annotation is used on individual methods.

With the default {@link Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} , {@code 0} disables the background sweep entirely: an expired entry is still never returned (it is discarded when it is next looked up), but it can keep occupying capacity until it is looked up or evicted to make room.

methods.name: impl
methods.signature: Class<? extends DaoCache> impl() default Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache.class
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the implementation class for the DAO cache.
methods.returns: the cache implementation class; defaults to {@link Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache}
contract: The implementation must implement {@link DaoCache} and declare a constructor that accepts two parameters: {@code (int capacity, long evictDelay)} .

The DAO proxy resolves that exact constructor signature when it creates the cache; a class that does not declare it fails DAO initialization with {@code IllegalArgumentException} (unlike the {@link #capacity()} / {@link #evictDelayMillis()} range violations, which fail with {@code UnsupportedOperationException} ).
If the implementation also implements {@link AutoCloseable} , an instance created for a DAO proxy that is then discarded, because another thread registered an equivalent proxy first, is closed.

types.name: CacheResult
types.javadoc_summary: Enables method-level result caching for DAO query methods.

methods.name: enabled
methods.signature: boolean enabled() default false
methods.javadoc_summary: Enables caching when set to {@code true} .
methods.returns: {@code true} to enable caching, {@code false} (default) to leave it disabled
contract: Enables caching when set to {@code true} .
The default is {@code false} ; set this element explicitly when the annotation should activate cache result handling.

methods.name: maxLiveTimeMillis
methods.signature: long maxLiveTimeMillis() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_LIVE_TIME
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the maximum time (in milliseconds) a cached entry can live.
methods.returns: the maximum cache entry lifetime in milliseconds; defaults to {@link JdbcUtil#DEFAULT_CACHE_LIVE_TIME} (30 minutes)
contract: Use a positive value: the built-in {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} rejects {@code 0} when storing a result (see the type-level documentation).

methods.name: maxIdleTimeMillis
methods.signature: long maxIdleTimeMillis() default JdbcUtil.DEFAULT_CACHE_MAX_IDLE_TIME
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the maximum idle time (in milliseconds) for a cached entry.
methods.returns: the maximum idle time in milliseconds; defaults to {@link JdbcUtil#DEFAULT_CACHE_MAX_IDLE_TIME} (3 minutes)
contract: If an entry is not accessed within this time, it expires and is removed.
This is useful for frequently accessed data that should expire if unused.
The entry expires when either {@code maxLiveTimeMillis} or {@code maxIdleTimeMillis} is exceeded, whichever comes first.
Use a positive value: the built-in {@link com.landawn.abacus.jdbc.Jdbc.DefaultDaoCache} rejects {@code 0} when storing a result (see the type-level documentation).

Usage Examples: 

 {@code // Expire if not accessed for 10 minutes @CacheResult(enabled = true, maxLiveTimeMillis = 3600000, maxIdleTimeMillis = 600000) @Query("SELECT * FROM user_sessions WHERE token = :token") UserSession getSession(@Bind("token") String token) throws SQLException; }

methods.name: minSize
methods.signature: int minSize() default 0
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the minimum size requirement for caching results.
methods.returns: the minimum result size to cache; the default {@code 0} means no minimum
contract:
Usage Examples: 

 {@code // Only cache if result has at least 10 items @CacheResult(enabled = true, minSize = 10) @Query("SELECT * FROM products WHERE category = :category") List findByCategory(@Bind("category") String category) throws SQLException; }

methods.name: maxSize
methods.signature: int maxSize() default Integer.MAX_VALUE
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the maximum size limit for caching results.
methods.returns: the maximum result size to cache; the default {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} means no maximum
contract:
Usage Examples: 

 {@code // Don't cache if result has more than 1000 items @CacheResult(enabled = true, maxSize = 1000) @Query("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE date >= :startDate") List findOrdersSince(@Bind("startDate") Date date) throws SQLException; }

methods.name: serialization
methods.signature: CacheSerialization serialization() default CacheSerialization.NONE
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies the serialization strategy for cache storage and retrieval.
methods.returns: the serialization strategy
contract: This determines how objects are copied when stored in or retrieved from cache.

Available options:

  • {@link CacheSerialization#NONE} (default) - No serialization, stores direct references
  • {@link CacheSerialization#KRYO} - Uses Kryo to deep-copy result graphs
  • {@link CacheSerialization#JSON} - Uses JSON round trips to create copies

With {@link CacheSerialization#KRYO} or {@link CacheSerialization#JSON} , collections, maps and populated optional/nullable wrappers are copied even when they implement {@link com.landawn.abacus.util.Immutable} .
Other top-level {@code Immutable} values are stored and returned as-is; their contents must be deeply immutable to avoid sharing mutable state.
Values without this marker pass through the selected serializer even if their Java types are immutable.
Unannotated methods used with the thread-local DAO cache select Kryo when its parser is available and JSON otherwise.

methods.name: cacheNestedResults
methods.signature: boolean cacheNestedResults() default true
methods.javadoc_summary: Whether calls made by this cached method may also use inherited type-level result caching.
methods.returns: {@code true} to preserve nested type-level result caching; {@code false} to suppress it

methods.name: filter
methods.signature: String[] filter() default { "query", "queryFor", "list", "get", "batchGet", "find", "findFirst", "findOnlyOne", "exists", "notExists", "count" }
methods.javadoc_summary: Specifies filter patterns for methods when the annotation is applied at the type level.
methods.returns: array of method name patterns to cache; the default targets common read methods: {@code query} , {@code queryFor} , {@code list} , {@code get} , {@code batchGet} , {@code find} , {@code findFirst} , {@code findOnlyOne} , {@code exists} , {@code notExists} , and {@code count}
contract: Specifies filter patterns for methods when the annotation is applied at the type level.
Each entry matches when the method name starts with that entry (case-insensitive), or when the entry matches the full method name as a regular expression.
This filter is ignored when the annotation is applied at the method level.
When the annotation is applied at the type level, methods whose names contain {@code "page"} or {@code "paginate"} (case-insensitive) are always skipped from caching, regardless of this filter.
